blocks.text: On Linux, Docker Engine runs containers directly on the host kernel. On macOS/Windows, Docker Desktop (and OrbStack, Colima, Rancher Desktop) runs a Linux VM and your containers live inside it; most "behaves differently on my Mac" issues come from that VM.

rows: Crosses VM boundary; slow for many small files
Apple Silicon = arm64; amd64 via emulation

items: Slow dev loop: bind-mounting .venv or node_modules. Keep dependencies in the image or a named volume; mount only source.
"Random" OOMs: the VM's memory cap, not your `--memory`.
arm64 images built on M-series Macs fail on amd64 servers with `exec format error`; build with `--platform linux/amd64` or multi-arch.
Windows: keep code in the WSL2 filesystem; NTFS mounts are slow and drop file-change events.
A setup that works on Desktop can fail on Linux CI because of real UID permissions.
Licensing: Desktop requires a paid subscription for larger organizations; Engine on Linux doesn't.

blocks.text: Q: "Why does my container work on my Mac but fail on the Linux server?" A: "Check what the Desktop VM hid: architecture (arm64 vs amd64), bind-mount UID permissions, host.docker.internal availability, and resource limits set by the VM rather than the container."

items: Desktop = containers inside a Linux VM.
Bind mounts are the main Desktop performance trap.
Apple Silicon builds arm64 by default.
Desktop masks UID issues that appear on Linux.
